xmldoc.short_description: Read an ISHNE 1.0 Holter ECG file into the neutral struct.

param_input_item.param_description: the path to the ISHNE 1.0 Holter file.
with 'Leads', the leads to keep, by name (a char or a cellstr) or by index, in the order asked; by default every lead.
a logical: 'Physical' whether to return the samples in millivolts rather than the raw integers (false by default), 'Data' whether to read the samples at all (true by default).

param_output_item.param_description: the neutral struct with the fields kind, path, samples (N x L), leadCount, leadCodes, leadNames, resolution, leadQuality, samplingRate, version, sampleCount, checksum, header (firstName, lastName, id, sex, race, birthDate, recordDate, fileDate, startTime, pacemaker, recorder), variableBlock and variableText.

description.p: The one reader of the ISHNE 1.0 Holter ECG binary format. It returns a domain-free struct: nothing in it assumes a diagnosis or any other interpretation.

An ISHNE file opens with the eight-byte magic 'ISHNE1.0' and a two-byte CRC, then a 512-byte fixed header, a variable text block, and the samples as signed 16-bit little-endian integers interleaved by lead. The whole file is read in one pass and every field cut from its bytes, because a misread of the little-endian samples or the per-lead resolution gives a signal that looks plausible and is wrong.

By default r.samples holds the raw signed integers the file carries, so a read followed by ishne.write is lossless to the bit. With 'Physical', true the samples are returned in millivolts, raw * resolution / 1e6, the resolution being the nanovolts per least significant bit each lead stores.

xmldoc.bibliography: Badilini, The ISHNE Holter standard output file format, Annals of Noninvasive Electrocardiology 3(3), 1998.

example_item.example_item_data: r = ishne.read('holter.ecg', 'Physical', true); plot((0:size(r.samples, 1) - 1) / r.samplingRate, r.samples(:, 1));
